correctness.rationale: The entire row-Gram generating kernel equals the product of local additive-character sums \(q\mathbf1_{\{x_i=y_i\}}-1\). The multiplicative-character Fourier transform on the product-one torus gives exactly \(Q^{-1}\sum_\gamma(qz)^{d-m_\gamma}(Q+z)^{m_\gamma}\), simultaneously for every degree; formal coefficient extraction produces both shell and band spectra. Positive coefficients prove precise rank and the shell-band range equality. For the last band the omitted top shell has eigenvalue Q^{-1}sum_gamma q^{d-m_gamma}; strict convexity classifies its unique maximum (trivial character) and balanced minimum, with exact orbit multiplicities. Every parameter and normalization is stated, including q=2. The actual bundled numerical checker passed 148 full direct spectral comparisons and 6 nonidentity-product cosets over prime and extension fields, maximum eigenvalue absolute error 1.9327e-12. The quantified conclusions follow from algebra, not from finite tests.

originality.rationale: Full primary sources were compared by mathematical implication rather than titles: Fraser-Rakhmonov treats the identical multiplicative Hamming variety but Fourier decay/Lp extension, not the additive low-interaction row-Gram spectrum. The published checksum-character result gives the rank occupancy threshold, which is expressly excluded from the novelty claim, and an unweighted integer character-band spectrum, not the weighted additive F-polynomial nor its optimal final-band eigenvalues. Results on observation Hamming shells, coordinate hyperplanes, and reciprocal frequency copies are different operators. The complete additive degree-family spectral polynomial and sharp last-band extrema remain uncovered by inspected statements; older implicit weighted harmonic analysis is a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: A historical MacWilliams, Hecke-algebra or weighted-code harmonic-analysis identity might give this additive occupancy polynomial under a different name; bounded searches cannot certify global priority.
The rank/surjectivity threshold is already covered by published multiplicative-character checksum sampling and must not be presented alone as new.

value.rationale: The finite-field multiplicative variety H_j is a natural model for restriction when uniform Fourier decay fails (Fraser–Rakhmonov, 2025). For this same object, the new theorem classifies all additive Fourier-frequency Hamming-shell and band singular values in every degree, rather than arbitrarily selected small instances. In addition to a complete nonnegative polynomial spectral law with exact multiplicities, it yields exact sharp last-band condition numbers and both endpoint eigenspace types for every field and dimension. Such information directly quantifies stable sampling and recovery on a natural group-coset variety, is not merely the previously known rank threshold, and supplies complete spectral invariant data usable in further Fourier sampling work.
